A single-pool process modeling a professor's workflow for evaluating a bachelor thesis from registration to final grade announcement. Demonstrates a wide range of BPMN elements in combination: message start event, event-based gateways, timer and conditional intermediate catch events, exclusive gateways, multi-instance loop tasks, signal throw event, data objects with input/output associations, and both message and terminate end events.

             targetNamespace="http://example.org/bachelorarbeit-bewertung">
  <process id="proc_bewertung" name="Bewertung einer Bachelorarbeit" isExecutable="false">

    <startEvent id="start">
      <messageEventDefinition/>
    </startEvent>
    <dataObjectReference id="dor_ba_angemeldet" name="BA ist angemeldet"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf1" sourceRef="start" targetRef="gw_xor_start"/>

    <exclusiveGateway id="gw_xor_start"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf2" sourceRef="gw_xor_start" targetRef="task_frist_eintragen"/>

    <task id="task_frist_eintragen" name="Abgabefrist im Kalender eintragen"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf3" sourceRef="task_frist_eintragen" targetRef="gw_event_wait"/>

    <sequenceFlow id="sf4" sourceRef="gw_event_wait" targetRef="catch_ba_erhalten"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf5" sourceRef="gw_event_wait" targetRef="catch_frist_ablauf"/>

    <sequenceFlow id="sf6" sourceRef="catch_ba_erhalten" targetRef="task_lesen"/>

    <sequenceFlow id="sf7" sourceRef="task_lesen" targetRef="gw_plagiat"/>

    <exclusiveGateway id="gw_plagiat" name="Plagiat?"/>

    <sequenceFlow id="sf12" name="traurig" sourceRef="gw_traurig" targetRef="task_musik_an"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf13"               sourceRef="gw_traurig" targetRef="task_termin_mitteilen"/>

    <task id="task_musik_an" name="Musik anschalten"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf14" sourceRef="task_musik_an" targetRef="gw_event_musik"/>

    <!-- Event-based gateway: music off after 10 min or when no longer sad -->

    <sequenceFlow id="sf18" sourceRef="catch_nicht_traurig"  targetRef="gw_xor_musik_join"/>

    <exclusiveGateway id="gw_xor_musik_join"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="sf19" sourceRef="gw_xor_musik_join" targetRef="task_musik_aus"/>

    <sequenceFlow id="sf20" sourceRef="task_musik_aus" targetRef="task_termin_mitteilen"/>

### Core Concepts

A Petri net is a directed bipartite graph used to model concurrent, distributed, or event-driven systems. It has three element types:

- **Places** (circles) represent conditions, states, or resources. At any point in time a place holds zero or more **tokens**. The distribution of tokens across all places is called the **marking** and represents the current system state.
- **Transitions** (rectangles) represent events or activities. A transition does not hold tokens; it consumes them from input places and produces them into output places when it fires.
- **Arcs** connect places to transitions (input arcs) or transitions to places (output arcs). Arcs between two places or two transitions are forbidden — the graph is strictly bipartite.

**Preset and postset:** The preset of a transition `t` (written `•t`) is the set of places with an arc into `t`. The postset (written `t•`) is the set of places with an arc out of `t`. The same notation applies to places.

**Firing rule:** A transition `t` is **enabled** under marking `m` if every place in `•t` holds at least as many tokens as the weight of the corresponding input arc, and every place in `t•` has enough free capacity to accept the tokens that will be produced. When an enabled transition fires, tokens are consumed from `•t` (according to arc weights) and produced into `t•` (according to arc weights), yielding a new marking `m'`.

**Condition/Event nets (B/E nets):** All arc weights and capacities are 1. A place is either marked (holds a token = condition true) or unmarked (no token = condition false). A transition fires only if all preset places are marked and all postset places are unmarked.

**Place/Transition nets (S/T nets, Petri nets proper):** Arc weights can be greater than 1, and places can hold multiple tokens and have explicit capacity limits. This allows modeling of resources, counts, and buffers."]

["## Petri Nets (PNML Syntax)

### Core Concepts

A Petri net is a directed bipartite graph used to model concurrent, distributed, or event-driven systems. It has three element types:

- **Places** (circles) represent conditions, states, or resources. At any point in time a place holds zero or more **tokens**. The distribution of tokens across all places is called the **marking** and represents the current system state.
- **Transitions** (rectangles) represent events or activities. A transition does not hold tokens; it consumes them from input places and produces them into output places when it fires.
- **Arcs** connect places to transitions (input arcs) or transitions to places (output arcs). Arcs between two places or two transitions are forbidden — the graph is strictly bipartite.

**Preset and postset:** The preset of a transition `t` (written `•t`) is the set of places with an arc into `t`. The postset (written `t•`) is the set of places with an arc out of `t`. The same notation applies to places.

**Firing rule:** A transition `t` is **enabled** under marking `m` if every place in `•t` holds at least as many tokens as the weight of the corresponding input arc, and every place in `t•` has enough free capacity to accept the tokens that will be produced. When an enabled transition fires, tokens are consumed from `•t` (according to arc weights) and produced into `t•` (according to arc weights), yielding a new marking `m'`.

**Condition/Event nets (B/E nets):** All arc weights and capacities are 1. A place is either marked (holds a token = condition true) or unmarked (no token = condition false). A transition fires only if all preset places are marked and all postset places are unmarked.

**Place/Transition nets (S/T nets, Petri nets proper):** Arc weights can be greater than 1, and places can hold multiple tokens and have explicit capacity limits. This allows modeling of resources, counts, and buffers.", '### PN-EX-06: Vending Machine (S/T Net — State Machine Structure)

When an item is dispensed, the machine returns to ready. An additional refill transition restores stock (5 items) when the machine is empty.
